title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Turkmenistan: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Turkmenistan: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Turkmenistan: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: Because Turkmenistan restricts and limits public online access to domestic government websites, civil registry manuals, notarial directories, and official legal gazettes, this guide relies on verified international statutory archives (WIPO Lex, FAOLEX, CIS Legislation, and HCCH) alongside foreign consular guidance [1] [2] [6] [8]. We set out the practical five-step sequence below, noting in particular that Turkmenistan is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention and requires full consular legalization for documents used abroad [6] [8].

steps.title: Confirm cause of death and register with local ZAGS
steps.html:
• Notify police and medical services if death occurs outside a hospital: Under Turkmenistan's health-protection framework and consular guidance, a treating doctor, police officer, or medical facility handles initial medical certification; where death happens outside a hospital, emergency medical services and police must attend to assess circumstances and verify identity [5] [8].
  • Consent rules for post-mortem examinations: Consent of the surviving spouse or next of kin (legally covering spouse, adult child, adult sibling, parent, or grandparent) is generally sought for a post-mortem except in suspected homicide, infectious disease, or pregnancy-related death; forensic reports pass through the prosecutor to ZAGS and family representatives [8].
  • Apply for the ZAGS death certificate: Once registered, next of kin or a representative holding a Power of Attorney apply at the local Civil Registry Offices (ZAGS) and State Notary Offices with the deceased's passport, residential details, kinship proof, and representative authorization [8]. Request multiple copies in Turkmen and obtain notarized translations into Russian or English [8].

steps.title: Arrange local burial, repatriation, and consular legalization
steps.html:
• Burial and foreign citizen authorization: Burial inside Turkmenistan requires engaging a local funeral provider and obtaining specific permission from municipal or state authorities if the deceased was a foreign citizen [8]. Where a foreign national's passport was submitted, consular officers coordinate directly with Turkmen migration and foreign ministry officials [7] [8].
  • Cross-border repatriation: Local funeral directors arrange embalming, sealed coffins, sanitary clearances, and customs export authorizations when transferring remains out of Turkmenistan [8].
  • Consular legalization instead of Apostille: Per the HCCH status table, Turkmenistan is not a Contracting Party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention [6]. Death certificates and notarial records intended for use abroad must undergo diplomatic consular legalization through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Turkmenistan and the receiving country's embassy [6] [7].

steps.title: Notify pension and social protection bodies
steps.html:
• Check state pension and survivor benefits: Under the Code of Turkmenistan on Social Protection of the Population (Law No. 340-IV of October 19, 2012, as amended through 2024), Social Protection and Pension Authorities of Turkmenistan administer state pension insurance, survivor pensions for dependents, and social allowances [4] [9].
  • Report cessation of payments: Submit copies of the ZAGS death certificate promptly to local social protection offices and state banks so pension or benefit disbursements are closed cleanly and eligible survivor benefits or funeral compensation are reviewed [4] [9].
  • Keep official translations ready: All domestic administrative filings take place in Turkmen (with Russian often accepted alongside notarized translation), so retain certified translators early [8].

steps.title: Complete estate succession after the six-month term
steps.html:
• Verify applicable Civil Code rules: Under Articles 1089 and 1256 to 1260 of the Civil Code of Turkmenistan (noting also the updated 2025 Civil Code codification recorded by FAOLEX), the estate comprises property rights and obligations at the moment of death [1] [2] [3].
  • Apply at the State Notary Office within six months: Under Articles 1256 and 1257 of the Civil Code, Civil Registry Offices (ZAGS) and State Notary Offices open inheritance files at the deceased's last place of domicile and issue a Certificate of Inheritance after six months from the date of opening of the inheritance (or earlier only where the notary holds definitive confirmation that no other heirs exist) [1].
  • Check wills and non-notarial local exceptions: Under Articles 1106 to 1120 of the Civil Code, written wills may be attested by a notary (or by an archyn where no notary operates), and Article 128 governs notarized Powers of Attorney for absent heirs [1].

steps.title: Transfer registered assets and settle accounts
steps.html:
• Notify banks, property registries, and utility providers: Present the State Notary Office's Certificate of Inheritance (and legalized foreign representative documents where applicable) to transfer property titles, close bank accounts, and settle outstanding utilities or tax obligations [1] [6] [8].
  • Preserve complete multi-copy records: Retain legalized copies of the death certificate, notarized translations, and notarial inheritance certificates, because re-issuing documents from abroad once local representation concludes is difficult [6] [7] [8].

contacts.name: Civil Registry Offices (ZAGS) and State Notary Offices
contacts.note: Local ZAGS offices register deaths and issue Turkmen-language death certificates; State Notary Offices handle powers of attorney, certified translations, and six-month inheritance certificates.

contacts.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Turkmenistan
contacts.note: Oversees consular affairs and diplomatic legalization of Turkmen civil and notarial documents for non-Apostille cross-border use.

contacts.name: Social Protection and Pension Authorities of Turkmenistan
contacts.note: Administer pension termination, survivor pensions, and social guarantees under the Code on Social Protection of the Population.
